c.tagline: Hokkaido's historic port of harbor-hill night views and morning-market seafood.

taxi.fareNote: Ride-hailing is very limited here; the GO taxi app can sometimes find a cab in the center, but most rides are hailed on the street or booked by phone. Fares are metered, and many taxis now take cards and IC cards.

emergency.note: 119 reaches fire and ambulance; 110 is police. English-speaking operators are limited, so having your location written in Japanese helps.

hood_desc: The historic hillside quarter climbing the slopes below Mount Hakodate, with its famous Hachiman-zaka slope, the Orthodox, Catholic and Anglican churches, Western-style former consulates and the ropeway to the night-view summit; the most scenic and atmospheric place to stay.

The waterfront district of the Kanemori Red Brick Warehouses, now full of shops, cafes and restaurants, with harbor promenades and easy tram access; a lively, walkable base between Motomachi and the station.

The central area around JR Hakodate Station and the Asaichi morning market, the city's transport hub and the spot for a fresh seafood and uni breakfast; the most convenient base for onward trains, trams and buses.

The neighborhood around the star-shaped Goryokaku fort and its viewing tower, a cherry-blossom park in spring, ringed by the city's everyday shops and dining; a quieter, more local base away from the tourist waterfront.
The seaside hot-spring resort district on the eastern edge of the city near the airport, lined with onsen ryokan and hotels with mineral baths; best for travelers who want to soak and unwind.

water.note: Tap water is safe and good quality.

transit.hours: Trams and city buses run from around 6:00 AM to roughly 10:30-11:00 PM; there is no late-night service, so taxis fill the gap after the last tram.
transit.note: Hakodate's compact old-fashioned streetcar (tram) system runs two lines linking the station, the bay, Motomachi and Yunokawa Onsen, backed up by an extensive Hakodate Bus network; the trams are the easiest way to reach the main sights.
transit.pay: Tap on with a national IC card such as Suica, Kitaca or ICOCA, or pay the driver in cash; a one-day tram-and-bus pass is good value if you plan several rides.

bus: Highway coaches to Sapporo and southern Hokkaido

transit.m: Airport shuttle bus to JR Hakodate Station (~20 min)

tip.r: Tipping is not customary in Japan and can cause confusion; polite, high-quality service is standard and already included.
